**3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d) **

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following two positions in the Department of Palaeontology & Historical Geology and the Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as of 01 January 2027

3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d)

(full time / part time)

Location: Frankfurt (Hesse)

Organizational units:

Department of Palaeontology & Historlcal Geology, Section Amber Research

Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology, Section Palaeomammalogy

Department of Palaeoanthropology, Section Mammalogy

Employment scope: Full-time / Part-time

Type of contract: Project-based, fixed-term for three years

Remuneration: Collective agreement of Hesse, TV-H E 9

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.

Within the framework of the project "SCRE3NED: Senckenberg Collection's RarEst – 3-dimensioNal Enhanced Digitisation", type specimens of exceptional scientific value (holotypes, paratypes and lectotypes) from various collections of the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt (amber, extant and fossil mammals, Messel fossils) are digitised using micro-computed tomography (μCT), synchrotron radiation-based micro-computed tomography (SRμCT), and digital photography. The aim is to produce high-quality, standardised and FAIR-compliant 2D and 3D datasets for research, collection management and science communication.

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Business Controller (f/m/d) within the TI CP Business Controlling team, you serve as a trusted advisor to the Compression Service Region Europe & Africa, supporting a business spanning more than 35 countries. Working closely with regional leadership, finance teams, and operational stakeholders, you provide transparency on financial performance, drive forecasting and budgeting processes, and enable data-driven decision-making across a dynamic and diverse business environment.

Beyond core business controlling, you contribute to key strategic initiatives, including Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), sustainability reporting, central function controlling, and high-impact transformation projects. By combining financial expertise with business acumen and cross-functional collaboration, you help drive sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation across the region.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Acting as the primary Finance Business Partner for the Compression Service Europe & Africa management team, providing financial transparency and actionable insights to support strategic decision-making
* Leading regional forecasting, budgeting, financial performance reviews, and financial planning & analysis activities across a network of more than 35 countries while identifying risks and opportunities
* Strengthening the Enterprise Risk Management framework and partnering with sustainability teams to support ESG initiatives, including EU Taxonomy reporting and compliance requirements
* Providing financial governance and controlling support for central functions, ensuring cost transparency, effective resource allocation, and sound financial governance
* Leading and supporting strategic projects and transformation initiatives, delivering financial insights, business case analyses, and value-creating recommendations
* Promoting process harmonization, digitalization, and automation to improve reporting quality, operational efficiency, and decision-making capabilities

What You Bring

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; an MBA or other advanced degree is considered an advantage
* Proven experience in controlling, financial planning & analysis (FP&A), business partnering, or finance leadership within an international environment
* Strong expertise in forecasting, budgeting, financial reporting, variance analysis, performance management, and financial governance, ideally complemented by knowledge of Enterprise Risk Management, ESG, or sustainability reporting
* Proven analytical and strategic capabilities with the ability to translate complex financial data into actionable business recommendations and influence management decisions
* Hands-on experience with SAP, financial planning systems, business intelligence tools, and Microsoft Office, combined with excellent stakeholder management and collaboration skills in multicultural organizations
* Fluent English skills; additional language skills are considered an advantage 

About the Team

In our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more. 

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

jobs.occupation: Research Software Engineer (all genders) HPC Code Performance Optimisation (Data Engineer)
jobs.description:
The German Climate Computing Centre (DKRZ) is the central simulation and data processing facility for the German climate and Earth system modelling community and one of the leading institutions in this field worldwide. DKRZ not only operates supercomputers of the highest performance class and one of the largest data and archive systems, but also participates in many national and international projects aimed at improving the software and infrastructure for climate modelling. Here we are offering a position as

Research Software Engineer (all genders)

HPC Code Performance Optimisation

Your tasks

DKRZ plays a significant role in a number of projects with the aim of advancing Earth System Modelling (ESM). This facilitates the advancement of scientific knowledge in the fields of Earth system modelling and climate research. In the context of the current development of digital twins of the Earth, it is necessary to adapt increasingly complex models and corresponding software to the most powerful HPC systems in Europe and ensure that those codes run stable and efficiently.

As a member of the team of Research Software Engineers (RSEs), you will collaborate with Earth System scientists to overcome technical challenges in high-performance computing (HPC) and software development. Your responsibilities will include further developing, testing and optimising existing coupled Earth System models. This will allow them to be extended with new components (e.g. ice sheet models) without compromising the efficient execution time. This is a key challenge, given the need to use resources effectively on current and future HPC systems. For this position, we are looking for candidates who are interested in the interdisciplinary implementation of Earth System models and who want to apply their programming skills to new challenges.

Qualifications / Experiences

•Academic degree in computer science, applied mathematics, computational physics/engineering or related fields with a focus on scientific computing

•Strong interest in and experience with HPC-systems and parallel programming with MPI/OpenMP

•Knowledge of programming with C/C++ and/or Fortran under UNIX/LINUX and scripting languages

•Experience in the use and programming of GPU systems for scientific applications is an advantage

•Experience in algorithms, data structures and design of scientific software is welcome

•Very good communication skills and knowledge of English

Employment conditions

We offer opportunities to work in interdisciplinary teams and have excellent connections to national and international research networks. In addition to specific implementation and support requirements from our users and project partners, your work will be characterised by the freedom to work creatively at the interface between applied computer science and the development of scientific applications. Attendance at international conferences, project meetings and hackathons facilitate further training and the presentation of your own results.

Our company is headquartered in Hamburg, but we are committed to creating a flexible working environment. We offer a remote working option, with the possibility of working from home up to 100% within Germany. Remuneration will be based on the candidate's qualifications according to TVöD-Bund. The ideal commencement date would be September 2026, although this is flexible and can be discussed on an individual basis. The position is funded by a third-party project, with a limited initial timeframe until the end of 2028.

Interested applicants are requested to compile a single pdf document containing a cover letter, a detailed CV and any additional documents (e.g. professional references). Applications must be submitted via the portalhttps://dkrz.softgarden.io/en/vacancies

Application deadline: Open until filled. Priority will be given to applications received by 23 August 2026

Questions? Dr. Hendryk Bockelmann (bockelmann@dkrz.de) will be happy to answer them in advance.

jobs.description:
KD Pharma Group is a medium-sized, internationally operating company headquartered in Bexbach, Saarland. We specialize in the manufacture of custom products that meet the diverse needs of the global market. In this role you will drive category strategies, lead supplier negotiations, and ensure continuous material availability across sites while achieving cost, quality, and delivery objectives. This role combines a strategic partner and a hands-on executor capable of managing sourcing strategies globally while also providing direct support to sites through day-to-day purchasing activities.

Aufgaben

Strategic Procurement Leadership

- Lead sourcing, negotiation, and contracting for Direct materials to achieve savings, quality, and supply continuity.
- Own assigned categories globally develop sourcing strategies, conduct market benchmarking, and drive competitive positioning.
- Lead supplier business reviews and category meetings, ensuring alignment between Procurement, Technical, and Operations teams.
- Identify and qualify new suppliers to enhance competitiveness and reduce supply risk.
- Collaborate with Finance to quantify savings impact on P&L and ensure transparency on cost drivers.

Negotiation & Commercial Strategy

Analytics & Performance

- Collaborate with the Senior Procurement Analyst to align methodologies and validate results but maintain ownership of strategic interpretation and decision-making.

Supplier Relationship & Risk Management

Cross-Functional Collaboration

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Employment scope: full time / part time options are available

Type of contract: initially limited to three years;

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A later permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation. A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile

- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field
- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations
- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage
- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management
- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team
- Very good command of German (B2)
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)
- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstances

Desirable skills

- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology
- Knowledge in research data management and databases
- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum work

We offer

- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology
- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work
- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities
- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications
- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.

For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/

For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de

Contact

Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung

Senckenberganlage 25

60325 Frankfurt a.M.

For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.

E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/x) Biology (Life Sciences) for Preclinical Imaging

Your salary will be based on TV-L

Your tasks
• Planning, conducting and analyzing the biological evaluation of newly developed PET and SPECT radiotracers
• Contributing to the establishment, optimization and
documentation of biological test systems and preclinical evaluation protocols

interpretation of results in close interaction with the other project partners

Your profile
• Completed university degree and Ph.D. in biology, life sciences, neuroscience, biochemistry, pharmacy or a related field
• Experience in preclinical imaging (e.g. small animal PET, SPECT, MRI, CT)
• Experience with animal models and experimental animal work is advantageous (FELASA-B or EU functions A, C, D)
• Experience with cell culture, in vitro assays, autoradiography, ex vivo analyses and BBB models is desirable
• Interest in radiopharmaceutical tracer development, molecular imaging and translational research
• Willingness to work with unsealed radioactive substances and to become familiar with radiation protection-related workflows
• Willingness to conduct biological and preclinical experiments within an interdisciplinary team
• Good written and spoken English skills
• Structured, independent and conscientious working style
• Ability to work in a team, strong communication skills and interest in interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, radiochemistry, biology, medicine and imaging

Our offer
• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.
• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.
• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.
• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.

Your future with us
We are one of the leading university hospitals in Germany and network research, teaching and health care at the highest level. That's why many things are a lot bigger for us: the spectrum of exciting development opportunities. The limitless openness with which specialists from all over the world work together here. Or our commitment as an employer to support all employees as best we can in reconciling their job with their goals and life situations.
This is the University Hospital of Cologne: Everything but ordinary.

Your future in detail
The Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. The postdoc position will initially be embedded for one year in the internationally funded IMAGESTRO project. There is an option of extension for another year. The focus of the work will be on the biological validation of newly developed PET or SPECT radiotracers.
The IMAGESTRO project aims to develop novel 18F-labeled PET tracers for the non-invasive imaging of estrogen receptors in the brain, to characterize them preclinically, and to translate them into human applications. The project focuses on the organic synthesis of suitable precursor and reference compounds, the development and optimization
of radiofluorination strategies, and the comprehensive analytical and preclinical characterization of the resulting radiotracers. The work will be carried out in close cooperation between the University Hospital Cologne and Forschungszentrum Jülich and offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of organic chemistry, radiochemistry, radiopharmacy, molecular imaging, biology and neuroscience.

Translation control in the hematopoietic system

Description

At the Institute of Transfusion Medicine and Cellular Therapeutics (Director: Univ.-Prof. Dr. Hannes Klump) we investigate mRNA-based reprogramming hematopoietic cells. Our aims are to generate and expand hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and to produce novel cellular therapeutics for patient care. We further investigate the regulation of translation in resting HSCs and during their differentiation into the hematopoietic lineages, as well as stimulation-induced changes to translation in mature hematopoietic cells. Our aim is to gain unprecedented and molecular insight into the underlying genetic programs and mechanisms and to leverage this understanding for the generation of novel therapeutic approaches.

In close collaboration with our research partners, we employ multidisciplinary approaches combining chemical synthesis, cell biology, molecular genetics, and biochemistry. We further offer an outstanding, international research environment with state-of-the-art facilities located in a newly constructed building that houses spacious clean rooms.

jobs.occupation: University Professor of Functional Genomics and Molecular Neurobiology (Professor/in - Hochschulen)
jobs.description:
Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region – home to the RMU Alliance formed by JGU, Goethe University, and TU Darmstadt – JGU can utilize its full potential and showcase its dynamic, innovative power. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching at JGU, in turn, paving the way for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its faculties and departments are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center, creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from all over the world.

The Institute of Developmental Biology and Neurobiology at the Faculty of Biology invites applications for the position of a

University Professor of Functional Genomics and Molecular Neurobiology

beginning at the earliest date possible. Salary grade W 2 LBesG | Civil servant (tenured)

Tasks and expectations:

We seek an outstanding candidate with a strong expertise in genetics and molecular biology, including the application of these approaches to the nervous system. Internationally recognised expertise and a strong track record of successfully securing external funding are required. Collaboration within the Faculty of Biology, the University Medical Centre, the Institute of Molecular Biology (IMB) and participation in current and future research consortia is expected.

The successful candidate will receive departmental positions and start-up funds and will be expected to establish an independent and internationally visible research program sustained by third party funding. Examples of further cooperation opportunities include: Institute of Quantitative and Computational Biosciences (IQCB) as well as collaborative research centres (e.g. CRC 1361 DNA Repair & Genome Stability; CRC 1551 Polymer Concepts in Cellular Function), the Research Unit FOR 5289 (From Imprecision to Robustness in Neural Circuit Assembly), or the Research Training Groups 4R (R-Loop Regulation in Robustness and Resilience) and GenEvo (Gene regulation in Evolution), the Carl-Zeiss-funded project for Interactive Bio-materials for Neural Regeneration and profile areas such as ReALity (Resilience - Adaptation - Longevity) or the Centre of Healthy Aging (further details here). The Rhine-Main Neuroscience Network (rmn²) offers further collaboration opportunities within the Rhine Main region.

Finally, the successful candidate will teach practical and theoretical courses in genetics, molecular biology and neurobiology at the Bachelor’s and Master’s level. We seek to increase the number of courses taught in English. Teaching is conducted in English and, in the basic Bachelor modules, in German. Applicants are therefore expected to be proficient in English and German. German language skills need to be acquired within five years of appointment. Participation in academic service is expected.

Requirements:

- In addition to the general requirements according to public services law, applicants must meet the recruitment requirements stipulated in Section 49 of the Hochschulgesetz of Rhineland-Palatinate. 
- In addition to the doctorate, a demonstration of excellent academic achievements is required. 

The state of Rhineland-Palatinate and JGU are committed to close personal mentoring of students and expect teaching staff to have a strong presence on campus. A cooperative, team-oriented and proactive work attitude, strong communication skills, and the willingness to assume responsibility – including further professional development in accordance with JGU’s leadership guidelines – is also expected.

Commitments of JGU:

JGU firmly supports making family and career compatible and promotes its employees’ further professional development. JGU welcomes qualified applications from people from diverse backgrounds. JGU aims to increase the number of women in research and teaching and therefore encourages female researchers to apply.

Candidates with severe disabilities or with equivalent status (as defined by section 2 subsection 3 of the Ninth Book of the Social Code, SGB IX) and appropriate qualifications will be given priority.

Please upload your complete application information and documents (CV, references, diplomas and certificates, as well as lists of publications and teaching activities, funding record, current research and future research plans, teaching concept) no later than September 30, 2026 via our portal with the following link: (https://berufungsportal.uni-mainz.de/datenabfrage/Genomics_Neurobiology)

The interview symposium is tentatively planned for November 2026.

For questions and further information, please contact the chairperson of the search committee Prof. Martin Heine (marthein@uni-mainz.de).

jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About the opportunity

As (Senior) Manager Direct Tax Compliance & Processes, you will act as a trusted business partner to management, driving efficiency and effectiveness across tax compliance, accounting, and reporting activities. You will play a key role in enhancing QIAGEN's tax compliance and governance framework, supporting our tax compliance insourcing strategy, and advancing tax quality and change management initiatives. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders while contributing to tax reporting, compliance, process optimization, and strategic tax projects across the DACH region.

Your tasks
* Further develop and enhance the Tax Compliance Management System while proactively supporting tax governance, tax quality, and change management initiatives.
* Support annual tax reporting at both legal entity and group level, including the calculation of tax positions and preparation of tax-related disclosures under US GAAP and local GAAP requirements.
* Manage direct tax return and compliance processes in collaboration with external advisors across the DACH region.
* Oversee additional tax compliance obligations within the DACH region and maintain the tax compliance calendar.
* Manage inbound and outbound withholding tax matters, including reporting and filing requirements, while identifying and implementing process improvements.
* Serve as a key business partner for Accounting, Treasury, Legal, Operations, and other internal stakeholders on tax-related matters.
* Support tax audits, tax planning activities, and corporate tax restructuring projects.

Your profile
* University degree in Business Administration, Economics (with a focus on Tax and/or Accounting), Tax Administration (Finanzwirt) or a comparable qualification.
* At least 5 years of relevant professional experience gained within an international advisory firm (e.g., Big 4) and/or the tax function of a multinational organization.
* Strong understanding of direct tax compliance, tax accounting, and tax reporting requirements.
* Proven ability to work independently with a high level of accuracy, diligence, and quality awareness.
* Experience with Microsoft Office applications as well as tax and ERP systems such as DATEV and SAP.
* Professional proficiency in English and German with strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Collaborative team player with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role)

We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

jobs.occupation: Robotics Manufacturing Engineer, Line Design, Geartrain (Automobil-Fachwirt/in)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

In this role you’ll support the design, construction, launch, and transfer of geartrain manufacturing lines and equipment used in Optimus Actuators. This role will prioritize successful design and launch of production line while maintaining maximum efficiency, production volume, and safety while validating performance and fully documenting all aspects of the project for handover to sustaining operations.  The ideal candidate will bring deep technical expertise in high-volume geartrain manufacturing lines and the successful introduction of new technologies to mass production line. They must demonstrate experience translating manufacturing requirements into efficient, detailed production line designs that are robust and practical to implement . In this position, you will take ownership of production line creation of specialized equipment from concept through line launch completion—defining performance requirements, running process flow simulations as needed to validate solutions grounded in first principles, and leading commissioning through final validation.

What You’ll Do

- Use CAD software and simulation tools (e.g., AutoCAD, FactoryCAD, or similar) to create 2D/3D models, floor plans, and detailed drawings that support both main production line and also supporting areas within Geartrain Manufacturing Scope
- Work with factory simulation/modeling teams to develop flow manufacturing constraints for new equipment development such as aisle sizing, incoming raw materials to the cell and work in progress areas between cells
- Install, commission, integrate and troubleshoot new equipment and tooling and support setup for manufacturing, including machines, peripheral equipment, tools, and automation systems
- Oversee the handover of commissioned lines to production teams, including operator training, documentation of procedures and manufacturing BOM, and resolution of issues during line launch
- Contribute to R&D efforts in equipment design and process development by integrating layout considerations, material flow, and facility requirements early in the innovation cycle to enable scalable and efficient manufacturing solutions
- Design and develop detailed cell and production line layouts for each gearbox, including placement of machinery and their integration to the mainline, workstations, material flow paths, utilities, and storage areas to optimize production processes and efficiency
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Factory, Infrastructure, Material Flow, Design, Manufacturing Eng., EHS personnel, and project&program leads) to integrate layouts into main factory design
- Ensure compliance with Tesla safety regulations, ergonomic standards, and lean manufacturing principles while evaluating new equipment and processes from R&D initiatives
- Evaluate data on production performance, material handling, and space utilization to recommend layout improvements that align with ongoing R&D advancements in equipment and manufacturing processes
- Design custom fixtures, tooling, and other structures that would be used in manufacturing cells as needed, providing detailed build to print models/drawings for fabrication

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Industrial Engineering or a related field (advanced degree or relevant certifications are a plus), or equivalent industry experience and evidence of exceptional ability
- Several years of experience in manufacturing or industrial engineering, with hands-on involvement in factory/plant layout projects
- Proficiency in layout design software, process simulation tools, and data analysis
- Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, material flow, ergonomics, and facility safety standards
- Experience designing layouts, mechanical equipment, fixturing, and tooling
- Knowledge in high speed gantry design including the pick and place into conveyor systems
- Knowledge in material flow analysis and basic knowledge about different industrial robots in high speed material transfer and pick and place applications
- Experience with SolidWorks CAD and PDM software. Familiarity with other CAD software (i.e CATIA, Siemens NX) also applies
- Experience with automation equipment, CNC equipment, heat treatment, assembly and end of line testing equipment
- Strong understanding of drafting standards and the application of GD&T (e.g., ASME Y14.5)
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

What to Expect

The Tesla Robotics Team designs and builds humanoid bi-pedal robots (Optimus) to perform tasks that are boring, repetitive, and dangerous for humans. As a CAE Engineer, you will guide the design of sensors and structural components using high-fidelity FE models grounded in sound engineering principles Working closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and manufacturing teams, you’ll analyze and optimize designs, challenge traditional CAE methods, and pioneer more efficient, accurate approaches. This role places you at the forefront of critical design and engineering decisions, shaping a robust and reliable humanoid robot that has never been executed before.

What You’ll Do

- Develop and analyze comprehensive Finite Element (FE) models for Optimus, from individual components to the full system
- Conduct static, dynamic, structural and MBD simulations to evaluate and validate the performance against key requirements for strength, stiffness, durability and sensing
- Build and refine simulation workflows to assess performance across diverse operating scenarios, automate processes, documentation, and tools to improve efficiency, accuracy, and repeatability
- Provide design guidance to world-class engineering teams, enabling data-driven product decisions
- Collaborate with Test Engineering to design and validate experiments, correlate test data with simulations, and enhance predictive modeling capabilities
- Establish and maintain modeling standards, methods, and best practices for current and future programs
- Material characterization and advanced modeling of structural and sensing components
- Plan and execute large-scale DOEs, creating ML driven surrogate models to extract insights to drive key design decisions

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
- Strong foundation in Engineering Mechanics, Computational Mechanics, Material Science, and Finite Element Theory and applications
- Demonstrated ability to guide structural, sensing, thermal, and mechanism designs through CAE, from concept to mass production, across robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics
- Expertise in building high-fidelity FE models at component, sub-system, and full-system levels
- Proficiency in linear and non-linear static, dynamic and modal simulations and experience developing multi-physics simulation workflows (e.g., thermal-mechanical, mechanical-electrical)
- Advanced knowledge in material characterization and modeling, including nonlinear elasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, and strain-rate dependent plasticity in Metals, Plastics, Polymers and Adhesives
- Proficiency in CAE Tools such as BETA CAE, LS-DYNA, Abaqus, ADAMS, COMSOL, OPTISTRUCT, Design Life, FE Safe
- Strong programming and data analysis skills in MATLAB, Python, or equivalent
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

We work with the cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Production, Sustaining, and Supply Chain) throughout the entire lifecycle of a product (from initial design through prototype development and into full production) to develop volume manufacturable designs and processes that will produce gearboxes. The role of the Gearbox Manufacturing Engineer is to support gearbox manufacturing process development to produce world-class gearbox prototypes and drive scalable production methods to high volume production. The ideal candidate takes pride in their work, has excellent engineering and physics fundamentals with hands on experience, is excited about manufacturing equipment and process development, does not shy away from a challenge, highly organized, has great attention to detail, and is able to work in fast paced development environment with analytical and practical engineering focus.

The role of the equipment control engineer is to support establishing to world-class production line for gearboxes and drive scalable design and production methods used to make “the machines that make the machines”. jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
As Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Affairs Obesity and Metabolic Health you will join a dynamic team dedicated to engaging with policymakers around the world to enable the access and uptake of life-changing pharmaceutical innovation. As part of the Public & Government Affairs function in the Corporate Affairs division, you will deliver integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change in particular areas of healthcare. At this time, we especially welcome applications from candidates with experience in policy shaping focused on Obesity and Metabolic Health, the therapeutic focus can shift in role based on business need.
This position is based at our Global Headquarters in Ingelheim, Germany.
Tasks & responsibilities

- As the Public & Government Affairs Lead for Obesity and Metabolic Health, in alignment with colleagues in the Corporate Affairs division, you will ensure we develop and implement integrated campaigns. In support of our established portfolio and future launches, you will establish alliances for awareness raising and targeted policy prioritization.
- One of your key tasks will be policy and stakeholder mapping to ensure the company has an informed position for key therapeutic areas within the Human Pharma business. You will lead on the creation of clear policy positions and support wider evidence generation to enable global and country teams to engage with policymakers.
- You will enable Public & Government Affairs capabilities and execution with a particular focus on the EU5, US, China and Japan.
- Moreover, you will support the Head of HP Public & Government Affairs to coach country teams in the development of clear strategic and tactical plans with measurable policy outcomes.
- You will be the main contact person for assigned Therapeutic Areas and other partners in the Human Pharma business. You will provide clear strategic counsel and be recognized as an expert in international health policy and country-level policy change.
- You will establish strong cross-functional relationships with teams including Communications, Market Access, Medical, Marketing, Legal and Compliance.

Requirements

- Master's degree in politics, Health Policy, Sciences, Economics, Law, or equivalent experience
- Several years of experience in a Public & Government Affairs role, potentially in-house, a consultancy or directly in Government
- Deep understanding of healthcare policymaking at a national and global level, including the role of the pharmaceutical sector in general and linked to specific therapeutic areas
- Business know-how to succeed in a global, matrixed organization, able to lead without direct management responsibility
- Demonstrable experience of delivering integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change
- Extensive experience in external networking to build meaningful relationships that drive (policy) change

Ultrasonic Acoustic Engineer (m/f/d)

Sound Propagation, Resonance & Biofouling Prevention

HASYTEC (Ultrasonic Tech GmbH, part of the ERMA TECH Group) develops and markets highly innovative ultrasonic technology that prevents biofouling on fluid-carrying surfaces. Our systems protect more than 300 ships, offshore platforms, and maritime installations worldwide against barnacles, algae, and mussels—efficiently, sustainably, and with minimal maintenance.

To strengthen our development team, we are looking for an Ultrasonic Acoustics Engineer who is passionate about understanding sound propagation, resonance behaviour and ultrasonic systems in complex maritime structures.

You will help develop the next generation of ultrasonic anti-fouling technology.

Our long-term goal is to protect not only piping systems and sea water equipment, but also large ship hull structures through controlled ultrasonic resonance fields.

Your responsibilities include:

- Analyze ultrasonic wave propagation in maritime structures and materials
- Investigate resonance behaviour in piping systems, sea chests, strainers, box coolers, propeller systems and hull structures
- Develop and optimize ultrasonic transducer configurations and installation concepts
- Plan, execute and evaluate laboratory experiments and onboard vessel trials
- Measure vibration behaviour and acoustic transmission using modern test equipment
- Analyze experimental data and derive practical design improvements
- Collaborate with hardware, software and mechanical engineering teams
- Coordinate technical activities with universities and research institutes

Technical Qualifications

- Degree in Physics, Acoustics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics or a related field
- Experience in one or more of the following: - Ultrasonics
- Acoustics
- Vibration analysis
- Resonance behaviour
- Signal processing
- Experimental testing
- Experience with laboratory measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers or vibration measurement systems
- Experience in data analysis using Python, MATLAB or similar tools
- Experience in maritime systems, fluid-carrying structures or piezoelectric technology is beneficial but not required
- Analytical and systematic working style
- Curiosity for understanding physical phenomena
- Hands-on mentality and enthusiasm for experimental work
- Ability to bridge theory and practical application
- Team-oriented mindset and initiative
- Our working language is English

What Makes This Role Unique

This is not a standard engineering position.

You will work on challenging acoustic problems involving sound propagation, structural resonance and ultrasonic excitation in real maritime applications.

The role combines physics, experimentation, onboard testing and collaboration with leading research institutions to develop sustainable technologies for the maritime industry.

What we Offer

- Work with a unique technology that contributes to more sustainable shipping
- A combination of laboratory research, practical testing and real-world applications
- High levels of responsibility and influence within a growing company at the forefront of sustainable technology
- Collaboration with international customers, universities and research institutes
- Modern equipment and short decision-making processes
- A technically strong and motivated, multi-professional international team
- employee benefits such as corporate pension schemes, bikeleasing and more

Research Associate / PhD Student (m/f/x)

excellent university degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering or a related field

an excellent working environment in an international team with many career development possibilities.

In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/x) in Machine Learning for Light-Induced Excited-State Dynamics in Materials

The successful applicant will join the research group of Prof. Silvana Botti at the Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems (RC FEMS) and the Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). The group develops first-principles and machine-learning methods to describe electronic excitations, light–matter interaction, and ultrafast dynamics in materials and at functional interfaces. The newly founded Research Center focuses on developing innovative materials and systems for sustainable energy applications. The center’s research areas include photovoltaics, thermoelectricity, energy storage, fuel cells, and sustainable chemical processes, among others. Its interdisciplinary approach involves collaborations between physicists, chemists, engineers, and material scientists to address the challenges of transitioning to a low-carbon economy. jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

PhD position (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholds

The work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: One of the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain a better understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles of nature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as it provides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physics deals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Among those hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the proton and the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created via collisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.

The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0 D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 years
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-06

Your tasks:

- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolution
studies within LHCb data analysis.
- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scattering
amplitudes.
- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS /
amplitude-serialization format.
- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.
Exchange with the experimental collaborations
[LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.

Your profile:

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.
- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity

with quantum field theory and scattering theory.

- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with

version control and reproducible workflows.

- Very good command of written and spoken English.
- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and in open,

reusable research software.

jobs.description:
The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The following full-time (38.5 hours/week) position is to be filled as soon as possible at the Center of Neurology of the University Hospital Bonn:

Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease (m/w/d)

The position is fixed-term until 30 September 2028 due to the duration of the research project.

Parkinson’s disease is usually diagnosed only after substantial neurodegeneration has already occurred. Subtle changes in movement, facial expression and speech may emerge years earlier, but current clinical assessments are not designed to detect and quantify them at scale. We believe that computer vision and multimodal AI can help close this gap - and that meaningful progress requires researchers who want to apply cutting-edge methods to a major clinical challenge.

Our goal is to develop objective and scalable digital tools for the early detection and monitoring of Parkinson’s disease. We combine video-based analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and limb movements with speech, touchscreen and wearable sensor data. A particular focus is on individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, who are at high risk of developing Parkinson’s disease or related neurodegenerative disorders.

The group of Prof. Dr. Michael Sommerauer at the Center of Neurology at the University Hospital Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will take a leading role in the development of the computer vision components of bradyMX, our multimodal digital motor assessment platform. The position is embedded in the ERC-funded Re-START PD research program and offers the opportunity to work with unique, deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts and longitudinal datasets. Rather than developing methods in isolation, you will work closely with clinicians and neuroscientists to translate methodological advances into tools that may improve patient stratification, clinical trials and, ultimately, the way Parkinson’s disease is detected.

Please submit your application as a single PDF, including: 

• a cover letter describing your scientific interests and motivation for joining the group 

• a curriculum vitae including a publication list 

• contact details for at least two referees

Your responsibilities:

- Lead the development of computer vision methods for quantifying subtle motor abnormalities from clinical video recordings
- Develop robust pipelines for human pose estimation, facial and body landmark detection, movement segmentation, tracking, feature extraction and automated quality control
- Design and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning models for the analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and upper- and lower-limb movements
- Investigate temporal modelling, representation learning and interpretable movement features for the detection and monitoring of early motor dysfunction
- Integrate video-derived features with complementary digital modalities such as speech, touchscreen tasks, inertial sensors and clinical assessments
- Evaluate model robustness and generalizability across participants, recording conditions, devices and international study sites
- Work closely with the clinical research team on study design, data collection, annotation strategies and the interpretation of model outputs
- Prepare scientific manuscripts, present results at international conferences and contribute to grant applications
- Support the supervision of doctoral, Master’s and medical students

Your profile:

- - A doctoral degree in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, biomedical engineering, medical informatics or a closely related discipline
- Strong experience in machine learning and deep learning for image, video or human movement analysis
- Excellent programming skills in Python and practical experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX
- Experience in one or more of the following areas: human pose estimation, motion tracking, action recognition, temporal modelling, self-supervised learning, multimodal learning or domain adaptation
- A sound understanding of experimental design, quantitative model evaluation and reproducible research practices
- Experience with version control and collaborative software development; knowledge of containerized workflows and high-performance computing is an advantage
- Interest in translating methodological advances into clinically meaningful applications; previous experience in Parkinson’s disease or medical research is welcome but not required
- A high degree of scientific curiosity, independence and commitment to rigorous research
- Strong communication skills and enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international environment
- Very good command of written and spoken English; German language skills are not required

What we offer:

The arbovirus research group of PD Dr. Beate Kümmerer at the Institute of Virology at the University Hospital Bonn (Germany) is looking for a highly motivated

PhD student (m/f/d)

to join our team and explore the fascinating biology of orthoflavivirus-host interaction in mosquitoes and vertebrates. The PhD position (65% E13 salary according to DFG recommendations), initially limited to three years, is advertisedwithin the framework of the DFG-funded CRC/Transregio 237 “Nucleic Acid Immunity” and is to be filled by January 2027.

The position is offered on a fixed-term basis until December 31, 2029.
Mosquito-borne RNA viruses, such as dengue, yellow fever, and Zika virus, cause severe disease outbreaks worldwide. As climate change drives the spread of mosquito vectors, the regions affected by these viruses continue to expand. Orthoflaviviruses have evolved multiple strategies to evade innate immune recognition, thereby promoting viral replication and pathogenesis. The project aims to elucidate how viral RNA structures and RNA modifications shape innate immune recognition. A particular focus will be the identification of mosquito proteins that recognize viral cap0 RNA and the characterization of viral immune antagonists in both mosquito and vertebrate hosts. We hope to gain mechanistic insights into virus-host interactions that support the development of innovative antiviral therapies and sustainable vector control strategies.

Methods: Molecular biology methods, cell culture and virological methods, RNA-protein and protein-protein interaction studies, gene expression analyses, cellular knock-down, as well as research involving mosquitoes.

Postdoc (m/f/d) in Endosymbiosis Research
Job-ID: J000000668
Working hours: Full time
Location: Düsseldorf
Start date: 01.01.2027
Limited until: 31.12.2028
Apply till: 21.10.2026
Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L
Organization: MathematischNaturwissenschaftliche Fakultät
Job Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Johannes Mayer offers the following PhD project:
Circulating myeloid cells, which include monocytes, dendritic cells and granulocytes, are short lived and continuously replenished by the bone marrow. Under non-inflammatory conditions, myelopoiesis follows relatively ordered differentiation routes that sustain circulating monocytes and granulocytes and seed tissue macrophage and dendritic cell compartments. Both mature cells and bone marrow progenitors have the capacity to rapidly reconfigure during local and systemic inflammation, with cell-cell communication cues from stromal, endothelial, and lymphoid niches helping to calibrate output and function.

Myeloid cell activation and exhaustion has both been described on a mature cell and progenitor cell level, leading to emergency myelopoiesis or hematopoietic halt/shock. Using single-cell and multi-omic profiling integrated with trajectory inference and ligand-receptor/network modeling, this project will establish a perturbation landscape of different myeloid cells and their progenitors in the context of different inflammatory cues using in silico modelling and in vitro validation.

PhD project: Defining Myeloid cell Ageing and its immunological impact on a single cell level

In our lab, we have established an integrated toolkit to study myeloid cell biology at single-cell resolution. Combined with datamining, LLM studies, in vitro activation and CRISPR/Cas9 perturbation screen, you will study the activation and exhaustion landscape of different myeloid cell types and their progenitors. In addition, you will work together with the team to characterize inflammatory models in vivo that span both systemic and local inflammation and track myeloid cell and progenitor activation and exhaustion over time.

This PhD requires a strong background in immunology, previous experience with both wet lab and dry lab work on a single-cell level and a willingness to work with in vivo animal models, including handling, experimental design and tissue processing and analysis.

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Johannes Mayer offers the following PhD project:
Trained immunity has recently been discovered as a novel mechanism of immune cell memory in innate immune cells. Different to the adaptive immune system, innate cells do not develop into antigen-specific long lived memory cells that can be reactivated. Instead, it was found that epigenetic and metabolic changes in stem cells and progenitors are transmitting previous information (e.g. from prior infections) and change the general activation status of future generations of innate immune cells. Especially monocytes have been studied in the context of trained immunity, but other cell types like neutrophils and even epithelial cells contribute to trained immunity.

These changes provide a more effective response to similar threats in the future, linked to pattern recognition pathways and cytokine production. As this re-activation is not antigen specific, it can also be triggered in response to other stimuli, potentially leading to broader beneficial but also detrimental effects. While trained immunity is not as specific or long-lasting as adaptive immune memory it still provides a faster, more robust reaction upon re-exposure in a non-antigen specific context.

PhD Project: Defining trained immunity in dendritic cells and their progenitors

In this PhD project we aim to study if dendritic cells also contribute to trained immunity. Dendritic cells play a fundamental role in antigen presentation and the priming of naive T cells. They are short lived and constantly replenished by stem cells within the bone marrow from where they are dispersed into tissues to sample and recognize pathogens. Several lineages of dendritic cells have been described, which originate from distinct progenitors.

In this project you will establish protocols on how to isolate and differentiate different DC progenitors in vitro and in vivo, using both human and murine samples. Furthermore, you will investigate principles of central and peripheral trained immunity and perform molecular single-cell and omics approaches and define the cellular, molecular and functional changes of dendritic cells. These changes will be carefully compared to monocytes, which have been well studied in trained immunity and assess differences between different dendritic cell lineages.

This PhD requires a strong background in immunology, previous experience with complex phenotyping of immune cells on a single-cell level and previous experience with either primary human or murine samples and cell isolation/characterization.

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Ilgiz Mufazalov in collaboration with Ari Waisman offers the following PhD project:
Regulatory T (Treg) cells are essential for controlling immune responses and preventing excessive inflammation. Currently, they are one of the most actively investigated cell types in immunology, with growing interest in their potential for treating autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Their importance was further highlighted by the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, which recognized discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance mediated by Treg cells.

Tissue inflammation is often associated with increased levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6), which can affect the function and stability of Foxp3⁺ Treg cells. How Treg cells survive and maintain their immunosuppressive function in an inflammatory environment remains poorly understood. Understanding the natural mechanisms that allow Treg cells to adapt to inflammation could help improve Treg cell-based therapies for inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

PhD Project: How interleukin-6 shapes regulatory T cells during inflammation

IL-6 signaling is mediated by its biologically relevant receptor, IL-6R. Our preliminary data show that IL-6R is expressed on Treg cell precursors in the thymus and on naïve mature Treg cells, but is downregulated on Treg cells at sites of inflammation. Treg cells isolated from IL-6-deficient mice, which lack IL-6 signaling during development, exhibit poor survival in IL-6-driven inflammatory conditions. These findings suggest that IL-6 signaling during Treg cell development may help establish the properties required for mature Treg cells to survive and function in inflammatory environments.

We hypothesize that Treg cells dynamically adjust their response to IL-6 during development and in peripheral tissues, allowing them to maintain immune suppression during inflammation. This regulation may involve changes in IL-6R expression and associated transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms.

In this project, we will investigate how IL-6 signaling shapes the function and fitness of Treg cells in inflamed tissues. We will use mouse models with cytokine overproduction or cytokine/receptor deficiency, as well as spontaneous and experimentally induced inflammatory models. Treg cell transfer experiments will be used to study their survival, stability, and suppressive function. We will combine multicolor flow cytometry (FACS), mouse immunology models, and sequencing approaches to identify the cellular and molecular mechanisms that control Treg cell fitness during inflammation.

The project is strongly immunological and will provide training in experimental mouse immunology, T-cell biology, flow cytometry, and molecular approaches.

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Sandra Schick offers the following PhD project:
Transcription is the first step in gene expression, governing cell identity, differentiation and response to environmental signals. Understanding the mechanisms behind the regulation of gene expression is essential because it is crucial for survival, and incorrect transcriptional regulation can have detrimental consequences ranging from reduced fitness to developmental defects and disease. Proper control of transcription requires a multitude of regulatory elements and proteins to act in a concerted fashion to organize the molecular machinery. Current models have proposed the role of dynamic assemblies, so-called transcription condensates (TCs), which constitute liquid-like environments that concentrate the necessary factors for efficient transcription at specific genomic locations. Our previous work showed that these condensates are heterogeneous and suggest a model wherein these transcriptional regulators form different condensates that are functionally specialized for distinct transcriptional stages. However, how they form, influence each other and transition into different stages remains unclear.

PhD project: The Role of Condensates in Priming Chromatin for Transcription Initiation

In this project, we will study the initial steps of transcription regulation and dissect the contribution of individual factors - such as co-activators, transcription factors, chromatin, chromatin modifiers, RNA polymerase II - for condensation, condensate properties and function. We will further study how they influence each other and how different types of condensates emerge. For this, we will use established reporter lines in combination with diverse microscopy approaches from live cell confocal to super resolution microscopy. We will additionally apply CRISPR technologies, genomics and proteomics approaches. Our cellular approaches will be complemented by in vitro experiments (Wittmann lab, IMB) and modelling (Speck lab, University of Stuttgart). This project is embedded within the collaborative research consortium SFB1551 (https://crc1551.com/, pending funding decision in November 2026).

The research group of Sandra Schick offers the following PhD project:
Transcription, replication and DNA repair represent key processes that act on DNA to ensure cell survival. As DNA is packaged into chromatin, chromatin remodeling, for example by BAF complexes, is required to coordinate and support genome maintenance processes. The BAF complexes exist in three different subtypes, each composed of multiple subunits. In previous work by us in collaboration with the Luck lab (IMB), we found that loss of either of the three BAF subtype-determining ARID subunits results in distinct vulnerabilities and resistances upon treatment with genotoxic or cell cycle-inhibiting agents. Since mutation of the ARID subunits is frequently associated with cancer, including colorectal cancer, we believe that these phenotypes are relevant to dissect molecular and cellular functions of the ARIDs and understand mechanisms that drive disease upon ARID perturbation. The Schick and Luck lab have developed jointly new computational and experimental techniques that enable the study of the ARID proteins in unprecedented ways.-mutated diseases.

PhD project: Deciphering the role of the BAF-associated ARID proteins in DNA mismatch repair and cell cycle control in colorectal cancer

ARID mutations in colorectal cancer are associated with microsatellite instability (MSI), usually caused by defective mismatch repair (MMR). We further observed MMR proteins in proximity to ARID1A. We thus want to use CRISPR engineered cancer cell lines and colon organoids to study the connection between ARIDs and MMR using compound screening and assessing the impact of ARID subunit loss on MSI and vice versa. In addition, we want to understand the impact of ARID mutations on cell cycle regulation in a cell type- and ARID-dependent manner.

In this project, the PhD candidate will apply bulk and single cell NGS and proteomics techniques in combination with genome engineering, compound screening and microscopy approaches using cell culture models, including colon organoid cultures. This project will be performed in collaboration with the Luck lab, who will complement this project by a structural proteomics approach. This project is embedded within the collaborative research consortium SFB1361 (www.sfb1361.de, pending funding decision in November 2026).
